prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an indoor counter scene where a counter and a red shopping basket containing items sit in the brightest foreground within arm's reach (~0.4–0.7 m in front and slightly right of the camera wearer), while a woman stands behind the counter on the left (~0.8–1.2 m away) and a glass display case on a table sits further back on the right (~1.5–2.5 m away, ~1–1.5 m to the right of the woman). In frames 1–4, the woman's head and right side are partly out of view at the upper-left edge and the counter and basket occlude her lower body and part of the chair behind the counter (~1.2–1.5 m away), before the camera turns left and tilts up in frame 5 to bring her full upper body into view as the wearer's hand enters at the bottom (~0.3–0.4 m away) next to the woman's left hand holding banknotes (~0.5–0.6 m away, within both people's arm's reach). The map clarifies the continuous distance gradient across the counter surface, the 3D layering of the woman's raised hands slightly in front of her dark-clothed torso, and the planar receding surfaces of the display case that are visually busy or low-contrast in RGB. However, the map is unreliable inside the perforated shopping basket—filling the holes as solid surfaces—and flattens the transparent glass of the display case and the open background doorway behind the woman (>3 m away) into uniform values, while providing no facial detail to tell where she is looking.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete regions across the scene: the woman on the left (~0.8–1.2 m away, labeled 'person'), a chair behind the counter between her and the basket (~1.2–1.5 m away, partly occluded by the counter and basket), a bottle inside the foreground basket (~0.5–0.6 m away, within the wearer's arm's reach), and the elevated display case on the right (~1.5–2.5 m away, ~1–1.5 m right of the woman). Across frames 1–5, as the camera pans left and shifts the basket toward the lower-right corner, the woman's mask expands from a left-edge cropped silhouette to a centered upper-body contour facing the camera wearer, while the display case mask shifts toward the right edge. Compared to the dark, low-contrast RGB regions, the segmentation map clearly separates the dark jacket-draped chair behind the counter from the woman's black shirt and isolates the upright bottle inside the cluttered basket. However, it is unreliable in class labeling and temporal stability—misclassifying the display case as 'tv', a snack packet in frame 1 as 'book', a counter device in frame 2 as 'suitcase', and the banknotes between the hands in frame 5 as 'cup', while completely missing the red shopping basket, the wearer's reaching hand in frame 5, and the distant background person in the top-left of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints for the woman standing ~0.8–1.2 m in front and to the left of the camera wearer, showing her torso oriented toward the counter and camera wearer with her elbows bent and hands raised at counter height within her arm's reach (~0.6–0.9 m from the wearer). In frames 1–3, because her head and right side are cropped out at the top-left border, only her left shoulder, left elbow, and raised right hand (magenta skeleton) are detected; as the camera turns left in frames 4–5, facial keypoints appear above her shoulders and her full upper-body skeleton (both shoulders, elbows, hips, and both hands) becomes visible, showing her facing the wearer while her head and eyes angle slightly downward toward the banknotes rather than directly at the camera. This map makes the exact 3D articulation of her fingers and the hidden arm segments beneath her featureless black sleeves explicit, which are difficult to discern in the dark RGB clothing. However, the pose map is unreliable when body parts are partially out of frame—omitting her torso in frame 1, collapsing her right hand into a sparse yellow wrist line in frame 4, and completely failing to detect the camera wearer's own hand reaching into the bottom of frame 5 (~0.3–0.4 m away) or the distant person in the upper-left background of frame 5, while offering no spatial information about surrounding objects or scene layout.
